_about: Spanish grammar notes, one per unit. The rule is in plain words; examples are the unit's own live sentences; conjugation tables come from Wiktionary at check time, never from memory.

notes.rule: Soy is how you say who you are, and eres is how you say who someone you know well is: both are forms of ser, the verb for who or what someone is. Every noun is masculine or feminine: un goes with a masculine noun (un hombre, un niño), una with a feminine one (una mujer, una niña). To say not, put no before the verb.
